unit: T3 UNIT F — a safe way to rehearse a credit pull (finding T3-13)
whatChanged: COMPLIANCE REVIEW REQUIRED — this changes credit-pull type behaviour. Staff can now practise a credit pull without any bureau being contacted. Sending `simulate: true` with the pull request runs the whole flow for real — the consent check, the identity check, the request record, the saved result, the follow-on events — and swaps out only the one line that talks to the credit bureau. The practice run is labelled "simulated" in five separate places, invents no scores and no accounts, and never changes the client's tier. Without that flag, a pull behaves exactly as it does today.

notes:
WHICH WAY EACH MISTAKE FALLS — you asked for this stated plainly.

  simulate absent            -> REAL pull. Unchanged. It has to stay this way: the live control-panel page posts without the field, and the c-00 diagnostic workflow calls the function without it. Making it required would break the live button today.
  simulate: false            -> REAL pull.
  simulate: true             -> simulated. Nothing reaches a bureau.
  simulate: anything else    -> REFUSED. Not real, not simulated, nothing stored. 'true' the string, 1, 'yes', 'on', 0, 'false', {} and [] all land here on purpose. A value the server would have to guess at is a value it refuses, because guessing 'real' would put a bureau hit on a real person nobody asked for, and guessing 'simulated' would hand a fake report to someone who wanted a real one.

So: it is IMPOSSIBLE to trigger a simulation by accident (only the exact boolean true does it, and nothing else in the system can set it). It is IMPOSSIBLE to get a real pull from a MALFORMED request for a simulation (that refuses). The ONE residual hole is a caller who intended to simulate and whose field never arrived at all — that reads as a plain real pull, and no code can tell it apart from someone who simply wanted a real pull. Closing that hole is a one-line change (make the field required at the endpoint) and it can be made the moment the control-panel page is updated to always send it. Your call, not mine to make.

NO NEW ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE, AND NO EXISTING ONE CHANGED. I did not touch CRS_ALLOW_LIVE or CRS_API_HOST behaviour, did not read any new variable, and did not print any value. Simulation is driven ONLY by the argument on the call. There is a test that sets CRS_SIMULATE, SIMULATE, CRS_DRY_RUN, CRS_SANDBOX and ADAPTERS_DRY_RUN all at once and proves the pull still goes out for real.

THE GATES STILL REFUSE FIRST, AND A SIMULATION RELAXES NOTHING. Tested: no consent -> refused before anything runs, simulated or not (a rehearsal is still a pull). No identity on file -> refused. CRS not configured -> refused. Production host with the live switch off -> still refused. A vendor test person offered to the production host -> still refused. The fence also re-runs the identity check itself, because that check normally lives inside the vendor call it replaces — skipping the call must not skip the gate.

WHERE THE STAMP GOES (five places, and the saved record is the authority — a repeat of the same request re-reads the label off the stored row rather than trusting whoever asked):
  1. the provider column reads crs_softview_simulated, not crs_softview
  2. the provider result id starts 'crs-simulated-bundle:' — visible in a database dump or a CSV export without opening the payload
  3. the saved payload has simulated: true plus a sentence saying no bureau was contacted
  4. both follow-on events carry simulated: true
  5. the pull-history reason column says SIMULATED
A real pull's saved payload and event payloads are byte-for-byte the same shape they have always been — no new keys — so every event ever written still means the same thing: no label means it was real.

THE TRAP YOU FLAGGED (client-detail.mjs:76). I checked every reader of the environment field before choosing. There are exactly two, both in client-detail.mjs (lines 76 and 242), and both skip on the word 'sandbox'. I made a simulated pull say 'sandbox' rather than invent a new word, because those readers do not read that field as 'which machine answered' — they read it as 'may I paint this as the client's real credit file', and 'sandbox' is the answer they already recognise. Inventing a third word would have made both of them paint a simulated result as real, and I cannot edit either file to teach them otherwise. The true host is not lost: it is saved beside it as hostEnvironment, and a new simulated flag is what tells a rehearsal apart from a genuine sandbox pull. And it does not blank anything — see blocked item 1.

TWO THINGS A REHEARSAL DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO, both because they would leave made-up data somewhere that cannot carry a label:
  1. It invents no numbers. The canned bureau answer has no scores, no accounts, no inquiries, no public records. Every step still runs, including the step that files accounts — there is simply nothing for it to file. Unknown scores stay unknown (null), never zero.
  2. It does not write the client's outcome tier. That column is one bare word on the real person's record with nowhere to say where it came from, and overwriting it would destroy the real value. The tier engine still runs, and its answer is still recorded on the simulated result row and in both events, where the label travels with it. A rehearsal will always produce MANUAL_REVIEW, because a file with no scores is what the engine was handed.

ONE EXTRA HAZARD I FOUND AND CLOSED. Reuse the same idempotency key across a rehearsal and a real pull and the same request row answers both — so a real pull could have been 'satisfied' by handing back a rehearsal that never contacted anyone, and the caller would be told a bureau answered when none did. That is now refused in both directions with code simulation_mismatch: a rehearsal cannot be replayed as real, and a real pull cannot be replayed as a rehearsal. You start a new request instead.

HOW I PROVED THE 6 FULL-SUITE FAILURES ARE NOT MINE. Two are worth your attention:

  (a) One of them names my endpoint: 'finance/crs-pull: a gate is referenced but its shape was not recognised'. I ran the journey generator's seven gate-detection patterns against the committed version of the file and against my version, side by side. All seven give identical answers, so the generator lands on the same 'unrecognised' branch before and after my change. PRE-EXISTING. The real cause is worth logging as its own finding: the endpoint calls the role check through an injected alias (requirePrincipalFn) rather than by its own name, and the generator's pattern only matches the plain name — so the published journey shows this credit-pull endpoint's role gate as unverified even though the gate is correct. The same failure names gifts/message-blaster, which is nobody's file in this batch. Fixing it belongs in scripts/journeys/extract.mjs, which I do not own.

  (b) 'docs/diagrams is in sync with the code' — the two stale files are README.md and event-flow.md. I built the diagrams in memory and checked: neither mentions crs-pull, simulate, or anything from my unit. My change adds no event, no route and no handler. Not mine.

The remaining four ('registration', 'the known-unfixed list is still true', the org-filter one, and the database-role one) are in files I do not own and have nothing to do with credit pulls. The database-role one is the known local-Postgres superuser condition CLAUDE.md section 12 already describes.
